decisions.issues: Minor only: the comrade's horse is drawn lying fallen beside him rather than standing riderless, which still reads as the script's beat. The cast list includes Keshavrao, but the beat comes after he is lost, so his absence is correct. I picked v08 over the otherwise identical v09 because its riders wear rust turbans with a red sash, which matches the Maratha cavalry dress in the bible. v09's white turbans could read as the Madurai troop. Nagoji matches his sheet: thick curled moustache, stubbled clean-shaven chin, gold stud, collar with side ring and torn ochre tunic. There is no painted text, and the riders are faceless backs. The sky at top left and the dust at bottom left give clear caption space over the memory stain, away from his face.
decisions.override: orchestrator: CONTINUITY.md standing rule, background Maratha riders in memory panels wear white or cream angarkhas and pagdis, never Nagoji's rust-red turban and sash; confirmed by the five-lens reviews r3 (continuity and rules). The selector's reading of the bible was wrong.

decisions.issues: v04 is clean and matches the script. It is a high angle down the hatch: Keshavrao's face is turned up with huge eyes and an open mouth, his manacled hands grip the top of the hatch, and below him his bare ankles are hobbled together on a rung in warm lantern light. Lightning and rain show above. He matches his sheet: short ragged hair, faint moustache, grey-brown torn tunic, empty iron collar with its ring, no ear stud. The wrist chain is clearly visible between his cuffs, which matches the 8.3 inset. There is no text or pseudo-text; the marks at the bottom are only wood grain on the cross-brace. Minor point: the chain's right end meets the base of the right thumb rather than exactly at the cuff, but it reads as one chain. One hobbled foot is hidden by the beam. 'Sahib!' can sit in the stormy sky at top left (about x 0.06-0.35, y 0.02-0.14) or on the dark deck boards at top right, clear of his face. Backup v03 has the same face and setting, with both hobbled feet visible, but his hands are spread too wide for a short chain and no wrist chain links the cuffs (one chain trails down, the other cuff has a loose ring). That weakens continuity with the 8.3 inset.

v05 is acceptable but not perfect. It is a distant wide shot of the closed, lantern-lit hold. The frame is tilted, and seawater surges knee-deep down the aisle between the pens. Collar-to-collar pen chains run taut and sideways, never vertical, and men brace against the boards. There is no painted text, no gore and no anachronism. Its weaknesses: the beat is calmer than the script asks, with no bodies thrown near-weightless. The extras are bare-chested in loincloths, while neighbouring panels 1.1 and 2.1 show ragged tunics. Nagoji and Keshavrao cannot be picked out, which is acceptable for a shot "from a distance rather than in detail". The single CAPTION fits on the dark, low-detail ceiling at the top left (about x 0.02 to 0.45, y 0.02 to 0.25). v06 is rejected. The far end of the hold is broken open to the sea, with daylight and a wall of surf pouring through the hull, so the closed hold is shown breached before the story allows it. Its prisoners are also drawn inconsistently with the Indian prisoners in the neighbouring panels.

v08 is clean enough to accept. It is an edit of v07, which r5 accepted, and it fixes v07's guard. The breeches are now dark brown, matching the guard's costume in 7.1 v13, where v07 had maroon. The thing hanging below his belt now reads as a pouch on a strap rather than a possible second leg and boot. The guard is seen from above and behind with his face hidden under the morion: buff jerkin, cross-belts, cream sleeves, sword, arms flung up, and five fingers on each hand. He drops through the gap between two flat treads toward the flood water at the ladder foot, which sets up 7.3. Nagoji matches the sheet and the ch3 row: thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud, long loose curly hair, hinged collar with its side ring, torn ochre sleeveless tunic and cream dhoti. Both bandaged fists grip one tread in manacles joined by one short chain, and the hands are sound. His cheek is pressed to the rail, eyes shut and face turned from the fall. The near arm is his left, bandaged to mid-forearm, so no brand shows. The setting matches 7.1, 7.3 and 7.4: a lamp-lit timber hold with barrels and a flooded floor, with lightning and rain only down the open hatch shaft. There is no text, blood, noose or anachronism. The panel is silent, so it needs no lettering space. Minor deviations, carried over from v07: a second metal ring still wraps the heel of the visible foot under the ankle cuff, which is small at print size and could be retouched. The guard is lit rather than the script's 'dark shape'. He tumbles jackknifed at the hips with his boots up behind his head, which still reads as a fall. Nagoji's treads sit on a second rail beside the main ladder rail, which only shows if you study it. v07 is an acceptable backup, but its maroon breeches clash with 7.1, and the dark shape below its belt could read as a stray boot.
